newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF can't rule out rate rise from Nomura, DKB move.
newsitem.headline: MOF can't rule out rate rise from Nomura, DKB move.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) cannot rule out the possibility of a rise in market interest rates as a result of the exclusion of Nomura Securities Co Ltd and Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank (DKB) from Japanese government bond (JGB) auctions, Atsushi Nagano, director general of MOF's securities bureau, told a news conference on Wednesday.

The ministry earlier announced that a ban on Nomura and DKB participation in JGB auctions would be extended until December 31, as part of punitive measures against the two firms for involvement in a racketeer payoff scandal.
Asked if the measures would affect JGB market rates, Nagano said: "Such a rise in the interest rate cannot be ruled out, theoretically."

Nagano said that there would be people who favour the sanctions, while others would oppose them due to the potential effect on interest rates. The ministry, however, chose to side with the former, he said.
